items.title: Standard One pupil dies after falling from 10th floor of PPR
items.summary: The incident occurred around 5.30pm while the boy was riding his bicycle outside his home. The boy's mother was informed of the incident by one of his friends. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: #NSTviral: Two men filmed riding on roof of moving Proton Wira
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Two men were filmed sitting on the roof of a moving Proton Wira, appearing unfazed as the car travelled along the road in a stunt that has drawn criticism on social media. The video, believed to have been recorded by a motorist travelling behind the car, showed a third person driving while the two men sat on the roof. The person recording the footage could be heard reading out the car's registration number and mentioning the location where the incident allegedly occurred.

items.title: Tree branch crushes lorry cab, driver escapes unhurt
items.summary: BATU KAWAN: A lorry driver escaped unhurt after a tree branch crashed onto the prime mover near Masjid Ar-Rayyan in Bandar Cassia today. The Fire and Rescue Department received an emergency call regarding the incident along Jalan Batu Kawan at 2.10pm. A team of eight firefighters from the Batu Kawan fire and rescue station was dispatched to the scene to carry out clearing operations.

items.title: Two Japanese climbers die on remote Himalayan peak in Nepal
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Rescuers recovered the bodies on Friday of two Japanese climbers missing for over a week on a remote Himalayan mountain, an expedition organiser said. The climbers were attempting the first summit of the 7,140-metre (23,425-foot) Gangapurna West in alpine style, but lost contact after Oct 15. Kumar Chhetri of Cosmo Adventure, which offered the climbers logistical support, said the search began after they failed to return to basecamp on Oct 18 as planned.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 23, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Sarawak polls next The Sarawak assembly will dissolve on Monday, with the state election to be held within 60 days. Waze ban possible Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim says the government may consider a nationwide Waze ban once suitable navigation alternatives are available. Govt appeals PN ruling The government has appealed a High Court ruling allowing Perikatan Nasional to resume political activities and contest the Melaka election.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Friday, Oct 23, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1562185]] [[nid:1562184]] [[nid:1562183]] [[nid:1562182]] [[nid:1562181]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Coffin, mock graves mark protest against 'killer road' on Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A series of accidents involving heavy vehicles, including a 12-vehicle pile-up that injured four people earlier this month, has renewed calls for urgent safety improvements along Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari. More than 100 residents from Alam Budiman and neighbouring housing areas staged a protest at the Jalan Alam Budiman traffic junction today, highlighting what they described as a "killer road". Gabungan Penduduk U10 residents' association chairman Badrul Hisham Shahbudin said the proposed flyover was needed to accommodate growing traffic volumes and improve safety for motorists from Puncak Alam, Puncak Perdana, Meru, Saujana Utama and surrounding areas.

items.title: Melaka polls: Rauf wants BN, Pas to work together, set aside prejudice
items.summary: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional (BN) election machinery in Melaka must set aside any reservations about Pas and work with the party on the ground. Also present were Pantai Kundor incumbent Datuk Tuminah Kadi and Melaka MCA chairman Datuk Lim Ban Hong. Rauf, who is also caretaker Melaka chief minister, said the state election would be important in determining the state's direction and gauging the coalition's strength ahead of the next general election.

items.title: Hamzah tells Kelantan Bersatu leaders to respect PN leadership
items.summary: Comparing PN to a team, Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin said its members should follow the captain's lead rather than act independently. Hamzah said Wawasan and Pas Kelantan had discussed political cooperation and preparations for the 16th General Election (GE16), including Wawasan's electoral prospects in the state. He said the talks covered broader political developments and cooperation within PN, rather than focusing solely on seat allocation in Kelantan.

items.title: Media Council warns against identifying minors in incident reports
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Media Council (MMC) wants media organisations to refrain from publishing details or unverified social media content that could directly or indirectly identify children involved in incidents as suspects, victims or witnesses. "Information that attracts public attention does not necessarily serve the public interest," it said. MMC acknowledged that incidents involving minors, particularly in schools, were matters of legitimate public concern.

items.title: Sarawak election dates to be decided at special EC meeting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting to decide key dates for the Sarawak election after receiving official notification of the state assembly from its Speaker. On preparations, Khairul Shahril said the EC had begun making logistical arrangements, preparing equipment, training election personnel and identifying suitable polling centres. On the EC's readiness, he said preliminary preparations included logistical arrangements, equipment supplies, training for election personnel and identifying suitable locations for polling centres.

items.title: Sarawak polls: Wawasan to discuss election plans with PN
items.summary: KOTA BHARU: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) will discuss its direction for the Sarawak election with Perikatan Nasional (PN) before deciding whether to contest. Its president, Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainuddin, said the party had members in Sarawak but would not make a decision unilaterally. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg announced this at Kompleks Satria Pertiwi in Petra Jaya today, after an audience with Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar at Astana Negeri.

items.title: Zetrix AI fails to resolve RM2bil sukuk breach, offers 789mil share options
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd has failed to reach an agreement with its sukukholders over a covenant breach involving its RM2 billion sukuk programme, prolonging uncertainty over the company's debt obligations. The setback came as the embattled technology group offered nearly 789 million share options to directors and employees at a 28 per cent discount to its closing share price of 7.5 sen today. Together, the four directors were offered 57.5 million options.

items.title: Court upholds lorry driver's 30-year jail term, 12 strokes for drug trafficking
items.summary: A three-judge panel led by Court of Appeal President Datuk Seri Abu Bakar Jais, together with Federal Court judges Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali and Datuk Azimah Omar, dismissed Ahmad Fahmi Mohd Hasnu's appeal against his conviction and sentence. Delivering the court's unanimous decision, Che Mohd Ruzima said the High Court judge had correctly applied the presumption of knowledge under Section 37(d) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, and that the appellant (Fahmi) had failed to rebut the presumption. On March 24 last year, the Court of Appeal dismissed Ahmad Fahmi's appeal and upheld the High Court's decision.

items.title: Zetrix AI redesignates Norraesah from executive chairman to chairman
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd has redesignated Datuk Norraesah Mohamad from executive chairman to chairman. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company announced the change as part of its latest boardroom update. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Body of baby girl found in Bangsar rubbish bin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The body of a baby girl, estimated to be around seven months old, was found at a waste disposal site in Bangsar here today. Brickfields police chief ACP Hoo Chang Hook said the department received a report regarding the discovery of the baby in a rubbish bin at 10.43am. Information can be channelled via the Kuala Lumpur Police Hotline at 03-2115 9999, the Brickfields Police Hotline at 03-2297 9222, or by visiting any nearby police station.

items.title: MCMC investigates Facebook’s failure to block livestream of teacher attack in Kuching, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is investigating Facebook’s failure to detect or block a livestream of an attack on a teacher in Kuching, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. The Madani government spokesperson said he would leave it to MCMC to investigate the incident before making any further comments. “MCMC is currently investigating the matter.

items.title: PN invited Bersatu to meeting as early as Sept 20, says Hamzah
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional (PN) had invited Bersatu to attend a supreme council meeting as early as Sept 20, but it was postponed due to a commitment involving the coalition chairman, said Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin. Hamzah said Bersatu had the right to attend the meeting if they wished to do so. "This is not the first time PN has invited Bersatu to a meeting.

items.title: Fahmi tells LLM, Prosignal to explain TuJu app glitches and fixes
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — The Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) and Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd have been asked to provide a detailed explanation of problems affecting users of the local navigation app TuJu, including their causes, technical issues and corrective measures. “The explanation from LLM and Prosignal is crucial to addressing users' concerns comprehensively, improving TuJu's reliability and strengthening public confidence in the local navigation app,” he told a post-Cabinet meeting press conference here today. Last Tuesday, the government encouraged Malaysians to use TuJu, developed by LLM, as an alternative navigation app.

items.title: Police rule out foul play in fatal Kajang helium tank explosion
items.summary: Kajang police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said preliminary investigations found no criminal elements in the incident, which occurred at 12.22pm. Naazron said police received a report on the incident at 12.58pm and rushed to the scene. "The victim was pronounced dead by Kajang Hospital medical personnel, who arrived at the scene at 12.35pm," he said.

items.title: Anwar apologises over Waze ban linked to Israel, says national security comes first (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has apologised if the decision to ban a navigation application owned by an entity linked to the Israeli regime causes any inconvenience to the public. “I apologise if the decision to ban this navigation application, which belongs to the Israeli regime, causes inconvenience to the public. Last Wednesday, the government decided to prohibit all civil servants from using the navigation application Waze, in order to safeguard government information and users' personal data against the threat of misuse by the Israeli regime.

items.title: UK tells public to keep three days' emergency supplies at home
items.summary: LONDON: The British government advised the public on Friday to keep three days of emergency supplies at home, a message it said had been hammered home by this week's PHP software glitch, as well as a record-setting summer of heat, drought and wildfires. The British government said the internet outage showed the importance of its newly launched "Be Ready" campaign, which advises the public to keep three days of bottled water and non-perishable food in the house. The government announced a new wildfire response plan that includes deploying military aircraft.

items.title: CelcomDigi files RM10bil sukuk programme to refinance debt, fund expansion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: CelcomDigi Bhd's wholly owned CelcomDigi Telecommunications Sdn Bhd has filed an Islamic medium-term notes programme of up to RM10 billion with the Securities Commission. AmInvestment Bank Bhd and CIMB Investment Bank Bhd have been appointed joint principal advisers, joint lead arrangers and joint lead managers. AmBank Islamic Bhd and CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd are the joint Shariah advisers.

items.title: Wawasan leaves Melaka seat allocation to PN leadership
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) is leaving it to the Perikatan Nasional leadership to decide how many seats the party will contest in next month's Melaka election. Wawasan president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainuddin said the party, as a PN component, would accept whatever decision was made. "As part of PN, we leave it to the PN chairman (Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar), who has mandated his secretary-general, Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, to handle discussions on seat allocation.

items.title: First Russian diesel from Putin-Trump deal heading for US, data shows
items.summary: NEW YORK: The first Russian diesel bound for the US following a surprise agreement reached between Moscow and US President Donald Trump is aboard a tanker heading for New York, ship-tracking data showed on Friday. Trump announced the dealthis month as part of his efforts to bring down soaring diesel prices ahead of November 3 US mid-term elections. Trump also waived parts of a new US sanctions law against Russia and threatened Europe with a US diesel export ban unless countries released more from their emergency reserves to help ease prices.

items.title: Abang Johari: Some GPS incumbents willing to make way for new faces in Sarawak polls
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 23 — Some incumbent Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) assemblymen have indicated they are willing to make way for new candidates in the coming state election, said Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg. He said the coalition’s line-up would comprise a mix of experienced and younger leaders, with new faces expected to feature. Earlier, Abang Johari announced that the Sarawak Legislative Assembly (DUN) would be dissolved on October 26 to pave the way for the next state election.

items.title: UK Royal Navy sailor appears in court charged under National Security Act
items.summary: LONDON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - A junior member of Britain's Royal Navy accused of collecting secret information and researching a website linked to Russia's foreign intelligence service appeared in a London court on Friday charged under the National Security Act. Young's role in the Royal Navy related to "warfare intelligence", prosecutors said at his first appearance earlier this month. The 24-year-old was allegedly "interested in a website set up by a foreign intelligence service", prosecutor Kelly Brocklehurst said at London's Old Bailey court on Friday.

items.title: Valvoline rolls out new motorcycle oils
items.summary: The Valvoline Champ range comprises fully synthetic, synthetic-blend and conventional formulations, with different grades designed for varying engine requirements and riding conditions. The wider motorcycle range includes Champ 4T Ultra Racing 10W-40, Champ 4T Extra in 10W-40 and 15W-50 grades, and Champ 4T Premium in 20W-40 and 20W-50 grades. For scooters, the lineup includes the fully synthetic Champ 4T Ultra Scooter 5W-40, alongside Champ 4T Extra Scooter and Champ 4T Premium Scooter in selected 10W-30 and 10W-40 grades.

items.title: Yinson Production, PTSC achieve first oil at Lac Da Vang field ahead of schedule
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Yinson Holdings Bhd's offshore production business unit, Yinson Production Offshore Pte Ltd, and PetroVietnam Technical Services Corporation (PTSC) have achieved first oil at the Lac Da Vang (LDV) field offshore Vietnam ahead of schedule. The floating storage and offloading (FSO) vessel, FSO PTSC LDV, achieved the milestone on Sept 27, 2026, ahead of the previously communicated fourth-quarter 2026 schedule, it said in a Bursa Malaysia filing today. Yinson Production chief executive officer Flemming Guiducci Grønnegaard said the achievement reflects the strong collaboration, technical excellence and shared commitment to safety among Yinson Production, joint venture partner PTSC, and its client, Murphy Oil Corporation.

items.title: Female tapir killed in suspected collision on LPT2 near Kijal
items.summary: Terengganu Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) director Dennis Ten Choon Yung said the department received information about the incident from the LPT2 management at 8am before four officers from the Kemaman district office were dispatched to the scene an hour later to investigate and conduct an inspection. He said the inspection found that the 200-kilogramme tapir suffered head injuries, several abrasions on its body and a fractured left hind leg, believed to have been caused by the collision. Dennis said the Bukit Kambing Forest Reserve was the nearest forest reserve to the scene, located about seven kilometres from where the tapir was found.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM OCT 23, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia closed higher on Friday amid global technology uncertainty, with domestic contract wins and earnings providing stock-specific opportunities. In the cryptocurrency market, Bitcoin fell to RM333,380. GNSWRVStn0A © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: DXN breaks ground on its first North African plant in Morocco
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: DXN Holdings Bhd has begun construction of its first manufacturing facility in North Africa, in Meknes, Morocco following approval from the Moroccan authorities. DXN group chief executive officer Prajith Pavithran said the project had progressed from an initial agreement to an approved development with construction underway. "Our first manufacturing plant in North Africa is a major step in DXN's global growth, and Morocco is central to how we will serve North Africa, Europe and the Middle East in the years ahead," said Prajith.

items.title: Man jailed 9 years for fatal wrong-way Federal Highway crash that killed 2 teens
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A 29-year-old businessman initially charged with murdering two teenagers in a fatal 2021 Federal Highway crash was sentenced to nine years' jail today after pleading guilty to culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The Shah Alam High Court amended the two murder charges against K. Devaaswin to culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304(b) of the Penal Code after the prosecution closed its case. High Court judge Datuk Bhupindar Singh Gucharan Singh Preet sentenced Devaaswin to nine years' jail on each charge, with both terms to run concurrently from his arrest on Sept 17, 2021.

items.title: Federal Court to hear former Negri Sembilan exco dismissal challenge on Dec 16
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Court will hear on Dec 16 a legal challenge by 10 former Negri Sembilan state executive council (exco) members against the state ruler's decision to revoke their appointments last month. Lawyer Datuk Wira Mohd Hafarizam Harun, representing the former exco members, and lawyer Marisa Regina Mohd Aris Rizal, representing the Negri Sembilan government, confirmed the hearing date after case management before Deputy Registrar Azaraorni Abd Rahman. The 10 are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Datuk Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.

items.title: Homestay turned scam hub in Melaka, 34 arrested
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has raided a homestay used as a call centre to defraud South Koreans through fake investment schemes, arresting 34 people. Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the operation yesterday also led to the arrest of two local men who allegedly received RM3,000 to guard the premises and supervise the workers. "Those arrested comprised 31 people from China, including 29 men and two women, a Taiwanese man and two local men, aged between 20 and 51.

items.title: Federal Court to hear Negeri Sembilan exco members’ dismissal challenge on Dec 16
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — The Federal Court has set December 16 to hear the legal bid filed by ten deposed Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (Exco) members to challenge the state ruler’s decision last month to revoke their appointments. The 10 are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Datuk Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah. They filed the notice of motion on October 14 and named the Negeri Sembilan State Secretary and the State Government as respondents.

items.title: ‘Completely false’: Waze rejects Malaysia’s data security claims after civil servant ban
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Navigation app Waze rejected on Friday Malaysia’s allegations that it could exploit users’ personal data, after the country banned civil servants from using the app over its Israeli links. Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the ban on Wednesday to “safeguard government information and users’ personal data against the threat of misuse by the Israeli regime”. “Claims that Waze collects sensitive government information or allows any entity to exploit personal user data are completely false,” a Waze spokesperson told AFP in a statement.

items.title: Ready for floods and extreme heat? North-east monsoon begins Oct 27, MetMalaysia warns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The 2026/2027 North-east Monsoon (MTL) is expected to begin on October 27 and continue until March next year, according to Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip. “Continuous strong north-easterly winds could also cause rough seas and rising sea levels in the South China Sea,” he said in a media statement today. As the monsoon enters its final phase, from January to March 2027, Mohd Hisham said rainfall was expected to decrease, particularly in the northern states of Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah.

items.title: Queen concerned over worsening mental health issues among children, teens
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, has expressed concern over the worsening mental health issues among children and adolescents, which have led to loss of life. This effort is specifically aimed at helping teens facing emotional distress, mental health problems and various life challenges. Istana Negara Grand Chamberlain Datuk Azuan Effendy Zairakithnaini led the discussion, which brought together several government agencies, including the Education Ministry, the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry, the Communications Ministry, the Royal Malaysia Police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission.

items.title: PTPTN sets RM50 minimum monthly repayment for graduates earning RM2,501 to RM3,000
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Graduates earning between RM2,501 and RM3,000 a month will only need to repay their National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loans at a minimum rate of RM50 per month, with the flexibility announced in Budget 2027. Deputy Higher Education Minister Adam Adli Abdul Halim said the loan repayment flexibility initiative is expected to benefit more than 400,000 people, helping to ease the financial burden on graduates who have just entered the workforce. He said graduates earning below RM2,500 a month would not need to begin repaying their loans until they reached the stipulated income threshold.

items.title: IGP: Police must treat seniors’ reprimands as lessons, not weakness
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail has reminded the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) personnel to maintain discipline and respect for senior officers to preserve the force’s strength and harmony. He said showing regard for senior officers appeared to be declining, raising concerns that this could weaken the police force and undermine its standing among other government departments and agencies. Mohd Khalid said police personnel should respect one another, accept feedback and different opinions, and recognise that they were not always right, adding that they should also remind one another of their responsibilities and respect senior officers to promote cooperation and solidarity within the force.

items.title: RoS challenges court stay on Perikatan deregistration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS) has filed an appeal against the High Court’s decision allowing Perikatan Nasional (PN) to suspend action by RoS to deregister the political coalition. Judge Azizan also allowed PN’s application to stay the implementation of RoS’ notice suspending all activities of the political coalition pending the court’s decision on its application for judicial review. On Oct 13, the court dismissed PN’s application for an interim stay of the RoS suspension notice but granted the political coalition leave to initiate judicial review proceedings.

items.title: Melaka polls: Perikatan seat talks with Umno to be finalised within days, says Tuan Ibrahim
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 23 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) is still negotiating to finalise seat allocations for the Melaka state election, with the coalition seeking one or two more seats on top of the seven discussed with Umno so far. PN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said talks were ongoing, and a final decision, including on any additional seats, was expected soon. Although the seven seats mentioned by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi are seats not won by Barisan Nasional (BN), we are still negotiating for one or two more seats.

items.title: Malaysia keeps Indonesia firefighting aid offer open, no local companies linked to forest fires
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — Malaysia’s offer to help Indonesia tackle forest fires causing transboundary haze remains open, with the government ready to provide firefighting assets if needed, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. Malaysia remains ready to provide assistance and assets if required,” he told his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here. Fahmi said the Prime Minister had expressed appreciation for the strong diplomatic ties between Malaysia and Indonesia and reaffirmed Malaysia’s willingness to assist in efforts to put out the fires.

items.title: Plan your commute: Severe weather warning for KL, Selangor, and nine other states this evening
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for several areas in 11 states and three federal territories until 6 pm today. In Kedah, the affected areas are Bandar Baharu, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Pokok Sena, Pendang, Sik, Kuala Muda, Langkawi, Kulim and Baling, while in Perak, they are Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim. In Kelantan, the warning covers Gua Musang, Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang and Pasir Puteh, while in Pahang, it covers Pekan, Kuantan, Cameron Highlands, Raub, Bentong, Lipis, Jerantut, Temerloh and Maran.

items.title: Corporate mafia task force’s terms of reference to go before Cabinet next week, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — The terms of reference for a special task force investigating allegations of a “corporate mafia” will be presented to the Cabinet next week, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. He said the task force’s findings would be made public within three months of the completion of the investigation, in line with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement in Parliament earlier this week. “The Prime Minister also informed the Cabinet that the terms of reference for the special task force that will investigate the findings related to the corporate mafia issue will be presented at next week’s Cabinet meeting,” Fahmi said at his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here.

items.title: UK-based Malaysian lawyer named Multilaw chair-elect
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Malaysian lawyer Joanne Vengadesan has made history after being elected chair of Multilaw, a global network of law firms spanning over 100 countries with 300 offices. The United Kingdom-based practitioner, who has 25 years of legal experience, was elected at Multilaw’s Global Conference in Prague earlier this month. Joanne said her international upbringing played a significant role in fostering her interest in being part of a global legal community such as Multilaw.

items.title: Fahmi says Malaysians can use any navigation app except Waze, including overseas alternatives
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — Malaysians are free to use any navigation application other than Waze, including alternatives developed locally or overseas, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. He said the government was not directing the public towards a single alternative amid concerns over Waze’s data security and ongoing efforts to improve the locally developed TuJu application. People can use various alternative navigation applications other than Waze,” he added.

items.title: BDS Malaysia backs civil service Waze ban, urges public boycott of navigation app
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — BDS Malaysia has welcomed the government’s directive banning civil servants from using Waze and its call for members of the public to stop using the navigation application. In a statement today, the organisation said it supported the directive, citing concerns that the use of Waze could compromise Malaysia’s national security and sovereignty. BDS Malaysia also urged the government to remain consistent in addressing national security concerns.

items.title: Architect charged with molesting senior cop’s son at Melawati gym sauna
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — An architect pleaded not guilty in the Ampang Magistrate’s Court today to a charge of molesting the son of a senior police officer at a gymnasium in Taman Melawati last Sunday. Datuk Saiful Anuar Abdul Aziz, 61, is accused of using criminal force against the 18-year-old victim with intent to outrage his modesty in a sauna room at a gymnasium in a shopping mall in Taman Melawati at 7.10 pm on Oct 18. Magistrate Siti Nur Ain Ariffin granted the accused bail of RM9,000 with one surety, imposed the additional conditions sought by the prosecution and fixed Nov 26 for mention.

items.title: Abang Johari calls for Sarawak state assembly dissolution on Monday
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 23 — The Sarawak State Legislative Assembly is set to be dissolved on Monday, Oct 26, 2026, paving the way for the 13th state election. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg announced the dissolution at a special press conference at the Satria Pertiwi Complex here this afternoon. He said the decision was made after obtaining the consent of Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar.

items.title: Anwar says nationwide Waze ban needs careful study first
items.summary: AMPANG, Oct 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today proposals for a nationwide ban on navigation app Waze required careful study, but did not rule out the possibility if capable local alternatives were available. “It must be studied what are the alternatives first, and if we find that local capabilities are good enough then we may consider prohibiting Waze altogether,” he told reporters after performing Friday prayers here. “Then a check showed Waze is governed only by Israeli laws.

items.title: Anwar acknowledges complaints about TuJu, urges users to be patient
items.summary: AMPANG, Oct 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today acknowledged complaints about local navigation app TuJu but urged users to be patient as its developer works to improve the service, amid the government’s ban on Waze for civil servants. “I feel our own people shouldn’t (criticise TuJu’s developer) harshly. Be patient.”

items.title: Malaysians spend more on eating out than cooking at home as health risks mount, says KRI
items.summary: The report, titled “From Income to Wellbeing: The State of Households 2026”, found that Malaysian households spent an average of RM902.70 a month on eating out, compared with RM875.80 on groceries. According to the report, the increase in food spending was more pronounced among the bottom 80 per cent of households, whose average food expenditure rose by nearly 1.5 times cumulatively between 2019 and 2024. “For the top 20 per cent (of households), the increase (in food expenditure) was less than 1.3 times,” it said.

items.title: Rafizi instructs lawyers to sue Ramanan, says minister’s graft claims crossed defamation line
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 23 — Former economy minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli has instructed his lawyers to begin defamation proceedings against Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan over corruption allegations the latter made against him yesterday. In a statement today, Rafizi said he had handed the video and transcript of Ramanan’s press conference to his legal team. Rafizi said Ramanan, who is also PKR vice-president, had made various allegations against him at the press conference, including accusing him of involvement in corruption.

items.title: Malaysians remain ‘happy’ as wages recover post Covid-19, but rising costs squeeze poorer households, says KRI
items.summary: The report, titled “From Income to Wellbeing: The State of Households 2026”, said median monthly household income reached RM7,017 in 2024, while labour force participation rose to 70.6 per cent that year. However, the report also noted that nearly half of Malaysian households (46.2 per cent) lived in 22 of the country’s 166 districts, where median monthly household income was below RM7,017. The report said household expenditure rose by more than 15 per cent among the bottom 70 per cent of the income distribution between 2019 and 2024.

items.title: Tighter rules for Malaysian dealers, agents, and accountants? BNM to review money laundering risks next year
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) will conduct the next iteration of the National Risk Assessment in 2027, enabling a deeper assessment of the money laundering and terrorism financing risks facing the Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions (DNFBP) sectors. Meanwhile, Marzunisham said the AML, CFT and CPF framework depends not only on strong laws and sound policies, but also on credible supervision and enforcement. Recent joint enforcement actions involving regulatory and law enforcement agencies reinforce this point.

items.title: Holy smoke: Massive ganja and heroin haul found in Klang house of worship
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 23 — Police uncovered drug trafficking at an unregistered house of worship in Klang during operations across Selangor from Oct 13 to 19. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said a local man who worked part-time as an assistant at the house of worship was detained to assist the investigation. In separate raids in Rawang and at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), police arrested seven individuals, comprising two local men, a local woman, three foreign men and a foreign woman, Shazeli said.

items.title: Budget 2027: Borrowers praise PTPTN repayment discounts and deferments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) borrowers have welcomed the repayment relief measures announced under Budget 2027, saying the deferment and lower monthly payments will help ease financial pressures, particularly among fresh graduates. Borrowers with no arrears who make regular repayments will also receive a 10 per cent discount. Jeremiah, who has maintained a consistent repayment record without arrears, also said the 10 per cent discount for regular repayments served as an incentive to maintain financial discipline.

items.title: Police: 19 reports lodged nationwide against man impersonating Selangor Raja Muda’s bodyguard
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 23 — An individual suspected of impersonating the personal bodyguard to the Raja Muda of Selangor to deceive members of the public has been found to have 19 police reports lodged against him nationwide. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said nine of the reports involving the 40-year-old man were lodged in Selangor in connection with fraud cases, with estimated losses totalling nearly RM700,000. He was speaking at a press conference on the achievements of the Selangor Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department at the Selangor police headquarters here today.
